name: Search Is a Content Problem
description:
Search Is a Content Problem: How Metadata, IA, and Governance Shape Discoverability

**About the talk:**

If you've heard users say they feel that your "search is broken" or that "they can't find anything", they're often pointing to a content problem. Search depends on clear titles, useful metadata, and strong content structure. When those pieces are weak, search results can't help your users. In this session, we’ll look at how to find and fix these problems. Lucy will share how audits, metadata reviews, and simple content changes can improve what users see in search. We’ll also look at how to prevent the same problems from coming back by setting clear content rules and standards.

**This will be a hands-on session in Mural.** You are invited to listen and participate at the level you're comfortable with.

**About Lucy Street:**
Lucy is a Senior Digital Strategist focused on making digital content easier to navigate and use. Her work has included just about every sort of of content strategy task. From complex site audits, microcopy writing, and content modeling. All the way to engaging stakeholders directly to promote better user experiences. She has over two decades of experience in human-centered design, which has served her well in all of her work. She focuses on building relationships with clients to build trust. Which helps bring empathy for all users into the room when decisions get made.

name: What it really takes to build an Internal Developer Platform with Backstage
description:
Backstage gives you a beautiful developer portal. But a portal is not a platform.

Behind every internal developer platform sits a long list of decisions and integrations. CI/CD. Observability. Environment management. Deployments. Access control. Backstage gives you the front door and a plugin model to wire it all together. The wiring is where the real work lives.

Join Kelsey Hightower and the OpenChoreo team for an honest look at what it takes to build a complete internal developer platform. We start with the vision: what developers should get from a platform, and what platform teams have to build to deliver it. Then we get concrete. We map the Backstage plugin landscape, show how vanilla Backstage has evolved, and count the glue it takes to turn a portal into a working system. We compare a few common approaches to observability and CI/CD, and show where each one leaves you.

We end with the decision every platform team faces. Build all of this yourself, or adopt something that ships it as one system, like OpenChoreo. For most teams, that means fitting new pieces into a platform they already run, not starting over. We won't tell you which is right. We'll make sure you know what you're signing up for either way.

You'll leave with a clear map of the moving parts, a realistic view of the effort involved, and a framework for the build-versus-adopt call.
